summary_out.changed: Kept the base aggressor-flow-gate's single 10s signed-flow gate exactly as-is and added one narrow override: when the base gate would SKIP on adverse flow, submit the order anyway iff mid has moved >= 1 tick (0.25 idx pts) in the order's favor during the last 3s sub-window inside the 10s flow window (mid tracked via a quote-tick deque fed by on_quote_tick).
summary_out.outcome: pnl -51.37% vs aggressor-flow-gate base (610.5 vs 1255.5 realized_pnl) — WORST of the island so far; sharpe 2.64 vs 5.59 (-52.9%); max_drawdown -0.0417 vs -0.0332 (worse 26%); trade_count 118806 vs 107198 (+10.83%, +11608 admissions); is_weighted_bps 0.04560 vs 0.04724 (-3.48%, BETTER — best IS of the island); vs_baseline_is_bps +17.27 vs +21.50 (largest IS improvement); slippage 0.0 on both. PnL prediction falsified; IS prediction confirmed — the IS-vs-PnL dissonance from g1l2 is now MUCH stronger.
summary_out.hypothesis: Required favorable mid-price evidence (>=1 tick over 3s, in the order's favor) before overriding the base's adverse-flow SKIP, expecting that filtering by an independent PRICE signal (not a flow surrogate like g1l1, not a population threshold like g1l2) would admit only adverse-flow-skipped trades whose path risk had already played out. The override is precisely identifying clean-arrival trades (IS bps improved sharply) — but those very trades are the WORST PnL contributors on the oracle's 30s horizon. Mechanistic read: an adverse-flow window with a brief favorable mid bounce is a short-term mean-reversion blip inside continuing adverse flow — adverse-selection bait, not a reversal. The base gate's value is in the SKIP itself; arrival-mid quality is anti-correlated with realized PnL on this strategy.
summary_out.next: DO NOT carry the price-confirmation override forward — it is the largest PnL regression of the island. Headline finding for migration: across THREE different override mechanisms (g1l1 flow-flip, g1l2 thin-window suppression, g1l3 favorable-mid confirmation), every attempt to LOOSEN aggressor-flow-gate's adverse-flow skip rule has regressed PnL, with severity correlated to the cleanness of the arrival-mid quality of the readmitted trades. IS bps is anti-correlated with PnL on this base — it must be treated as a diagnostic, NOT an objective. Most promising directions for g1l4 pivot entirely AWAY from loosening: (a) stack a SECOND independent gate on top of the base (tightening, not loosening, e.g. a volatility or time-of-day filter that fires independently of aggressor flow); (b) leave entry decisions alone and modify the post-fill behavior (e.g. conditional accelerated exit when the original flow-signal re-asserts adversely after a fill); (c) accept the base as a strong local optimum on its entry-gate dimension and explore a different lever entirely (sizing as a function of flow conviction, e.g. half-size on borderline cases vs full-skip).  Cross-island generalizable insight: when a base's gate is well-tuned, the trades it rejects are NOT free P&L — they are rejected for reasons that may be invisible to arrival-price diagnostics.
